title: PointHeartFiniteStageEquivalences
statement: Fix D, l different from the characteristic, and an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l. For every finite coefficient subfield A of Omega, the specified rational point-heart functor H^0 Fib_A is full, faithful, additive, and essentially surjective onto finite-dimensional A-vector spaces. The specified common-stage point-heart functor H^0 Fib_Omega has the same three functor properties and is essentially surjective onto finite-dimensional Omega-vector spaces. No exactness properties are included in this lemma. All specified functors and structures are those of [def-zl-point-heart-finite-stage-data].

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero input; steps 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 of lem-zl-point-heart-finite-stage

proof.text: First work at a finite coefficient field $E$. The source standard halves are the isomorphism closures of the integral halves. Sections on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact and satisfy $H^r\Gamma(s,K)=\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^rK)$. Rationalization of module complexes is exact: tensoring with $E=\mathcal O_E[1/\varpi_E]$ is module localization (the identification sends $x\otimes a/\varpi_E^n$ to $ax/\varpi_E^n$), and localization preserves exact sequences. Thus the specified $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}(K)=\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ preserves both standard halves. The standard module truncations preserve bounded finite-dimensional cohomology, so restrict to $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$. Both categories consequently have bounded standard t-structures. The specified fibre functor is an exact equivalence by the point-fibre theorem.

proof.text: Apply the t-exact truncation-comparison theorem to this exact functor: $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}\tau^{\le m}\cong\tau^{\le m}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$ and likewise for $\tau^{\ge m}$, preserving their canonical maps. It also reflects the halves. Indeed, if its value on $K$ is in degree $\le0$, the value on $\tau^{\ge1}K$ is zero; full faithfulness reflects zero objects, since $\operatorname{id}_X=0$ whenever its image is zero. Hence $\tau^{\ge1}K=0$, which is the source degree-$\le0$ criterion. Use $\tau^{\le-1}$ for the other half. For any target heart object choose a preimage under the derived equivalence; these two arguments put that preimage in the source heart. Restricting the full-faithfulness bijections therefore gives an equivalence of these two hearts.

source.place: 1.3.3–1.3.6, canonical truncations and their universal properties; reflection argument written here

proof.text: On the standard heart inside $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, degree-zero cohomology is an equivalence with finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces. Explicitly, for a representing complex $C$ concentrated in cohomology degree zero, the canonical maps $C\leftarrow\tau^{\le0}C\to H^0(C)[0]$ are quasi-isomorphisms: the first retains all nonzero cohomology, and the second is the cycles-to-cohomology projection in degree zero. Their natural roof supplies the canonical identification. The degree-zero embedding is fully faithful by the cited derived-single theorem, and $H^0(V[0])=V$. This proves both full faithfulness and essential surjectivity of $\omega_E=H^0\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$, with precisely the canonical truncation identification, rather than a chosen splitting of a complex.

proof.text: Every object $X=(E,K)$ of $\Sh_c(s,\Omega)$ has an actual finite-stage heart model. Put $M=\tau_E^{\ge0}\tau_E^{\le0}K$. It lies in $\Sh_c(s,E)$. Constructible truncations and their canonical maps are computed at finite stages, so $(E,M)$ represents $\mathcal H^0(X)$. Since $X$ is in the heart, the two canonical truncation maps identify $\mathcal H^0(X)$ with $X$; write $e:(E,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ for the resulting isomorphism. This uses the heart condition only in the common-stage category; it does not assert that the original integral or rational representative $K$ was already in the heart. Subsequent extension of $M$ remains in the heart because the truncations commute with finite scalar extension.

We now check the $\Omega$ equivalence directly, without identifying the raw common-stage category with an idempotent completion. Replace two heart objects by finite-stage heart models from step 5, over fields $E,E'$. At a common $L\supset E,E'$, step 3 identifies their Hom group with the linear maps between the corresponding finite-dimensional $L$-fibres, and step 4 identifies the transition maps with scalar extension. The Hom definition is the directed colimit of exactly these groups. In bases over $E$ and $E'$, an $\Omega$-linear map is a finite matrix; its finitely many entries lie together in a finite $L\subset\Omega$, by the union and compositum assertions for finite subextensions. A matrix over $L$ becoming zero over $\Omega$ already has every entry zero. Hence this Hom-colimit maps bijectively to the $\Omega$-linear Hom group. Every finite-dimensional $\Omega$-space is isomorphic to $\Omega^d$; the finite equivalence at $\mathbf Q_\ell$ realizes $\mathbf Q_\ell^d$. This proves essential surjectivity too. By definition of common-stage cohomology its value is $H^0\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Omega}$, with the scalar comparison of step 4.
